title: Acute myocardial infarction on YouTube - Is it all fake news? (Enfarte agudo do miocardio no YouTube)
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of Portuguese-language YouTube videos on acute myocardial infarction (10 search terms x first 100 results = 1,000 videos screened; 242 eligible). Two medical observers coded each video for the presence of clinical/scientific inaccuracies against an external standard, with kappa 0.84 for that item. 79/242 (32.6%) contained inaccuracies, and a separate top-10-per-term subsample of 100 videos gave 22.0%. These are shares of items in a sample judged inaccurate, with stated denominators -> CONTENT. HONCode and DISCERN indices are additionally reported and coded QUALITY. Article body is in Portuguese; quotes are given verbatim with English translations.

estimates.country: Portugal (searches run on a computer connected to the Internet in Portuguese territory; videos restricted to the Portuguese language)
estimates.measure_type: % of eligible Portuguese-language YouTube videos on acute myocardial infarction containing clinical/scientific inaccuracies
estimates.denominator: 242 eligible YouTube videos, from 1,000 screened (the first 100 results for each of 10 Portuguese search terms) after excluding duplicates (345), irrelevant (316), non-Portuguese (106) and audio-less (24) videos
estimates.definition: A video entered the numerator if the coders recorded the presence of a clinical/scientific inaccuracy (the type of clinical/scientific error was transcribed); examples given include a video claiming that certain foods can replace percutaneous coronary intervention and one claiming that AMI symptoms appear a month before the event
estimates.misinfo_def: "A informacao foi analisada quanto a presenca de imprecisoes, anotando-se o tipo de incorrecao clinica/cientifica." [The information was analysed for the presence of inaccuracies, noting the type of clinical/scientific error.] The paper frames these as "desinformacao" / "fake news".
estimates.page_loc: Resultados, 'Qualidade dos videos', p. 6; also Abstract: 'One third of the videos (n=79) contained inaccuracies'
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two medical resident observers with specific training (IF and DM) assessed every eligible video; disagreements resolved by consensus among three investigators (IF, DM, JBA). Intra- and inter-observer reproducibility assessed with Cohen's kappa on a random 10% subsample (25 videos): the presence of clinical/scientific inaccuracies had the HIGHEST inter-observer agreement, kappa 0.84 (0.62-1.00); video topic the lowest, 0.63 (0.39-0.87). Intra-observer reproducibility re-assessed after more than one month.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The by-SOURCE and by-TOPIC inaccuracy figures in Table 2 and in the text (e.g. 'formadores individuais 33 (41)', 'sinais e sintomas (n = 46, 58,2%)') are percentages of the 79 INACCURATE videos, not of each source's or topic's own videos - the source column sums to 100% across sources. They are therefore a composition inside the misinformation set, not prevalence, and I extracted none of them. This is an easy trap: read naively, '33 (41)' looks like 41% of independent-instructor videos being inaccurate, but 33/95 = 34.7%. (2) 'Videos com origem em sociedades cientificas e instituicoes de saude ou governamentais nao apresentaram quaisquer imprecisoes' [Videos from scientific societies and health/governmental institutions presented no inaccuracies at all] is a verbatim 0% for two named source classes (n = 14 and n = 10 videos), but those source-level denominators are small and are not stated as shares; not extracted. (3) 'One third of videos was irrelevant' (316/1,000 excluded as irrelevant) is a relevance judgement, not a falsity judgement, so it is not a misinformation prevalence despite the abstract framing it as part of 'desinformacao'. (4) 'Apenas um video (0,4%) apresentou concomitantemente boa qualidade ... sem imprecisoes' [Only one video (0.4%) simultaneously had good quality and no inaccuracies] is a joint quality-and-accuracy share, not a misinformation share. (5) The 19-video sensitivity analysis excluding personal-experience and news-chain videos ('apenas tres apresentavam imprecisoes') reports counts without a stated percentage. (6) Correlations between inaccuracies and views/likes (r = 0.285 and r = 0.289, both p < 0.001) support a positive exposure gradient but carry no share. (7) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY between abstract and results for the audience split: the abstract says videos 'were addressed to the general population (n=202, 83.5%)' while the Results say 'A maioria dos videos destina-se ao publico em geral (n = 199, 77,7%)'; likewise 39.0% vs 39.3% for independent instructors. This does not touch the extracted inaccuracy figures but is a sloppiness signal.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Sampling frame: YouTube searched between 7 May and 5 August 2019 from a computer in Portuguese territory, not logged in and with cookies cleared; 10 Portuguese search-term combinations, results ordered by relevance with no other filters, first 100 results per term retained (1,000 videos). Exclusions: irrelevant (316), duplicated (345), no audio (24), non-Portuguese (106), with 33 videos meeting multiple exclusion criteria; multi-part videos counted once (42); 242 eligible. Coding procedure: two trained medical resident observers (IF, DM) rated every eligible video for source, topic, target audience, typology, presence of clinical/scientific inaccuracies, HONCode (0-8) and DISCERN (0-5); disagreements settled by consensus among three investigators. Reliability: Cohen's kappa on a random 10% subsample (25 videos) - presence of clinical/scientific inaccuracies kappa 0.84 (0.62-1.00), the highest of any parameter; video topic 0.63 (0.39-0.87), the lowest; intra-observer reproducibility re-tested after more than one month; all agreement described as good or excellent. Statistics: SPSS 22, chi-square/Fisher, t/ANOVA, Mann-Whitney/Kruskal-Wallis, two-sided alpha 0.05. Authors' limitations: video assessment is subjective; short search window with top-100 turnover (mitigated by a median 823-day age since upload); no viewer demographics available; search terms not exhaustive (abbreviations such as 'EAM' not searched).
